gpt-oss-120b.description: Recommended default — OpenAI's open-weight gpt-oss-120b, the exact model OVHcloud's own getting-started guide uses for every code sample (docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/ai-machine-learning/ai-endpoints-getting-started, retrieved 2026-09-28), and the most fully documented model on the public catalog card (ovhcloud.com/en/public-cloud/ai-endpoints/catalog/gpt-oss-120b/, retrieved 2026-09-28). That card's own "Supported Features" list names exactly Function calling, Reasoning and Streaming; its "Output Formats" list names raw_text, json_object and json_schema. The card's Python example builds the request with `Authorization: f"Bearer {os.getenv('OVH_AI_ENDPOINTS_ACCESS_TOKEN')}"` against https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1/chat/completions, and reads a `reasoning_effort` generation parameter (low/medium/high) plus a `reasoning_content` response field — the basis for capabilities.thinking. No sign-in or API key was used to read any of this; it is all public documentation plus the unauthenticated GET on /v1/models. contextWindow and maxOutputTokens are the live, unauthenticated /v1/models response's own context_length/max_completion_tokens fields for this id (GET run 2026-09-28, HTTP 200). Pricing is that same response's per-token USD pricing (prompt/completion fields) converted to $/MTok; the EUR-denominated marketing catalog card quotes the same model at €0.08 in / €0.4 out per Mtoken, consistent with the API's USD figures at roughly current EUR/USD. No live request of any kind (chat, streaming, tool call) was made against this model — the entry is docs- and roster-verified only; see evidence.liveMatrix (null).

gpt-oss-20b.description: OpenAI's smaller open-weight gpt-oss-20b. Not individually probed; roster-verified fallback.

errorRules.message: Invalid or revoked OVHcloud AI Endpoints access token. Check {apiKeyEnvVar}. Get one at {setupUrl}

instructions: 1. Visit: https://www.ovhcloud.com/en/public-cloud/ai-endpoints/ and click Start now, which signs you in to (or creates) an OVHcloud Public Cloud manager account

2. In the manager, open Public Cloud > your project > AI & Machine Learning > AI Endpoints, and add a payment method to the project — OVHcloud states that projects in Discovery mode (no payment method) cannot use the service
3. Create an AI Endpoints API access token in that section; it is shown only once, so store it yourself, and note it can be given an expiration date and revoked
4. Set {apiKeyEnvVar} in your .env file (the vendor's own docs name this exact variable)
setup.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1, documented as "compatible with the OpenAI specifications" (docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/ai-machine-learning/ai-endpoints-getting-started). Several models (both Qwen3Guard classifiers, stable-diffusion-xl, the four NVIDIA Riva TTS voices) are billed at €0/free, but the account itself requires a payment method on the Public Cloud project before any API key can be used — OVHcloud's own docs: "projects in Discovery mode (without a payment method) cannot use the service." A very limited anonymous tier also exists (2 requests/minute per IP per model, undocumented auth shape) but is not what {apiKeyEnvVar} configures. Authenticated rate limit is documented as 400 requests/minute per project per model; over that returns HTTP 429. This catalog entry covers only the chat-completions models; OVHcloud AI Endpoints also serves speech-to-text (Whisper), text-to-speech (NVIDIA Riva), image generation (Stable Diffusion XL) and embeddings (bge-m3, bge-multilingual-gemma2, Qwen3-Embedding-8B) models on the same platform, which are out of scope for this Tier-2 chat-completions integration.
